children: A hand-rolled velocity-Verlet layout living inside the Graph Renderer — the physics whose feel is the subject of the Graph Comparison.
Force Simulation is the layout engine inside bp-graph.js, the Graph Renderer. Rather than pull in a physics library, it integrates node positions with a hand-written
step run once per animation frame. Three forces act each tick:
— nodes push each other apart (an N-body term) so the graph spreads.
— edges from the Content Edges Table pull connected nodes together.
— a gentle pull toward the middle, with the Graph Traversal root
so the whole layout stays anchored.

The repulsion strength, spring stiffness, and center pull are exactly the parameters the Graph Comparison exists to evaluate against Obsidian's graph. Obsidian's layout has a recognizable settle and spacing; matching that feel — not just the dot styling — is what makes the side-by-side fair. Get the constants wrong and Barkpark's graph reads as "almost Obsidian," which is the failure mode the fixture catches.

The simulation never touches the server. The Graph View pane ships a static data-nodes/data-edges payload once; from there the Graph Renderer owns every frame, stepping this simulation locally. Orphan Nodes feel only repulsion and center pull (no springs); a Phantom Node participates in layout but is drawn muted.
